assessment_summary: The statement is false. The complete bipartite graph K_{2,4} is a valid counterexample because it is 2-connected and Eulerian, but not Hamiltonian.
counterexample:
Consider the complete bipartite graph $K_{2,4}$ with vertex parts $U=\{u_1, u_2\}$ and $W=\{w_1, w_2, w_3, w_4\}$, and all edges between $U$ and $W$.
- It is a finite simple graph with 6 vertices.
- It is Eulerian because it is connected and every vertex has an even degree: $d(u)=4$ for $u \in U$ and $d(w)=2$ for $w \in W$.
- It is 2-connected because removing any single vertex leaves the graph connected. (Removing a vertex from $U$ leaves a star graph centered at the other vertex in $U$, and removing a vertex from $W$ leaves $K_{2,3}$.)
- It is not Hamiltonian. Since it is a bipartite graph, any cycle must alternate between vertices in $U$ and $W$. Thus, a Hamiltonian cycle (which must visit all 6 vertices exactly once) would require the two parts to have equal size, but $|U|=2 \neq 4=|W|$.
